decisions.id: W80-1 circular arc of 2.5 widths' radius
decisions.summary: swept_bend draws a circular arc of radius 2.5 channel widths tangent to both runs, cut-back radius x tan(turn/2), replacing a quadratic whose cut-back was 2.5 widths
decisions.why: 0054's drawing page: 'About 2.5 channel widths in radius'. The implementation moved to the research, as the request and FR-004 ask. The unit test re-run by this reviewer (4 passed); a 20-degree turn's cut-back 1.76 at radius 10 is 10 tan(10 deg).

decisions.id: W80-2 radius capped at 35% of the shorter run
decisions.summary: the RADIUS (not the cut-back) is capped at 0.35 x min(l0, l1)
decisions.why: 0054: 'A bend's radius is capped at 35% of the straight run on either side'; the shorter run is 'either side'.

decisions.id: W80-3 hairpin cut-back within 90% of the run
decisions.summary: where the capped radius would put the tangent point past 90% of the run, the radius is tightened to 0.9 run / tan(turn/2); claimed UNRESEARCHED
decisions.why: It draws a radius under 0054's figure. The literal rule cannot be drawn there: at r = 0.35 run the cut-back passes the run's whole length near 141 deg and is unbounded at 180 deg, and a tangent point past the run's far end has no straight to stand on. It serves 0054's own purpose for the cap ('Two neighboring bends never swallow the straight between them'), and a smaller radius still meets the cap, an upper bound. The 90% margin is labeled this project's guess at the point of change and in the Decisions Recorded row.

decisions.id: W80-4 junctions and turns under 8 deg left sharp
decisions.summary: round_channel_joints' choice of which joints to round is unchanged
decisions.why: 0054's claim already names it; the wave changes only how a selected bend is drawn.
